facts.statement: Claosaurus is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur named "broken lizard" because its fossils were found in an odd position.
facts.quote: Claosaurus ( ; Greek κλάω, klao meaning 'broken' and σαῦρος, sauros meaning 'lizard'; "broken lizard", referring to the odd position of the fossils when discovered) is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period (Santonian-Campanian) of what is now North America.

facts.statement: The only known valid species of Claosaurus is Claosaurus agilis.
facts.quote: The type and only known valid species is Claosaurus agilis.

facts.statement: While traditionally classified as an early hadrosaurid, a 2008 analysis placed Claosaurus outside the Hadrosauridae clade as the closest non-hadrosaurid relative within Hadrosauromorpha.
facts.quote: Traditionally classified as an early member of the family Hadrosauridae, a 2008 analysis found Claosaurus to be outside of the clade containing Hadrosaurus and other hadrosaurids, making it the closest non-hadrosaurid relative of true hadrosaurids within the clade Hadrosauromorpha.

facts.statement: The size of adult Claosaurus is uncertain due to insufficient fossil remains consisting of a minority of skull and partial skeleton.
facts.quote: Because of the insufficient fossil remains ("minority of skull and partial skeleton"), the size of an adult Claosaurus remains uncertain.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz estimated the length of Claosaurus at 3.7 meters and its mass to be similar to that of a lion.
facts.quote: However, Thomas Holtz gave a length estimate of 3.7 m and a mass estimate as that of a lion.

facts.statement: Claosaurus was an herbivore, like other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Like other hadrosaurs, it was an herbivore.

facts.statement: Fossils of Claosaurus were first found in 1871 in the Niobrara Formation near the Smoky Hill River in Kansas, including partial skull fragments and an articulated postcranial skeleton.
facts.quote: Evidence of its existence was first found in the Niobrara Formation near the Smoky Hill River in Kansas, United States in the form of partial skull fragments and as an articulated postcranial skeleton both found in 1871.

facts.statement: Claosaurus was originally named Hadrosaurus agilis in 1872 but was renamed Claosaurus agilis in 1890 after major differences from Hadrosaurus were identified.
facts.quote: Originally named Hadrosaurus agilis (Marsh, 1872), it was placed in a new genus and renamed Claosaurus agilis in 1890 when major differences between the specimen and Hadrosaurus came to light.

facts.statement: A second species, C. annectens, was named in 1892 but was later reassigned to the genus Edmontosaurus.
facts.quote: In 1892, Marsh named a second species, C. annectens. It was later reassigned to Anatosaurus and then Edmontosaurus, where it is currently.

facts.statement: G. R. Wieland named a third species, C. affinis, in 1903 based on remains from the Pierre Shale of South Dakota.
facts.quote: G. R. Wieland named third species C. affinis in 1903, which he compared to C. annectens.

facts.statement: The remains used to describe C. affinis were found in the Pierre Shale of South Dakota in association with the giant sea turtle Archelon.
facts.quote: C. affinis was founded on remains from the Pierre Shale of South Dakota, found in association with remains of the giant sea turtle Archelon.

facts.statement: Joseph Gregory corrected the holotype status of C. agilis in 1948 by identifying three toe bones from the right foot in the Yale collections.
facts.quote: This was corrected by Joseph Gregory in 1948, who found three toe bones from the right foot of a large hadrosaur in the Yale collections that had comparable preservation to the Pierre Shale turtle remains and were associated with labels in Wieland's handwriting.

facts.statement: A 2004 review by Jack Horner and colleagues considered C. affinis a dubious hadrosaur, reporting its type material as lost and noting only a single toe bone remained instead of the three described by Gregory.
facts.quote: C. affinis was considered a dubious hadrosaur in the 2004 review by Jack Horner and colleagues. They reported its type material as lost, although they also reported the remains as only including a single toe bone, instead of the three toe bones described by Gregory.

facts.statement: Reports of gastroliths in Claosaurus are based on a probable double misidentification of the specimen.
facts.quote: Reports of gastroliths, or stomach stones, in Claosaurus are actually based on a probable double misidentification.

facts.statement: The specimen thought to have gastroliths was originally misidentified as Claosaurus by Barnum Brown in 1900 because Edmontosaurus annectens was then considered a species of Claosaurus.
facts.quote: Barnum Brown, who discovered the specimen in 1900, referred to it as Claosaurus, because E. annectens was thought to be a species of Claosaurus at the time.

facts.statement: Claosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous Period (Santonian-Campanian) in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Claosaurus ( ; Greek κλάω, klao meaning 'broken' and σαῦρος, sauros meaning 'lizard'; "broken lizard", referring to the odd position of the fossils when discovered) is a genus of hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period (Santonian-Campanian) of what is now North America.

facts.statement: Claosaurus agilis lived approximately 80 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in North America.
facts.quote: Claosaurus agilis (gr. "lagarto roto ágil") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Claosaurus de dinosaurio ornitópodo hadrosauroide, que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 80 million years ago, en el Campaniense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Claosaurus is from the Coniacian to the Campanian, between 89.8 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Coniacian to Campanian (89.8 to 72.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Claosaurus was a bipedal herbivore with a slender body, long hind legs, and small forelimbs.
facts.quote: Claosaurus fue un herbívoro bípedo que presentaba un cuerpo delgado, con patas traseras largas y extremidades delanteras pequeñas.

facts.statement: Claosaurus measured about 3.5 meters in length and weighed about 475 kilograms, featuring a slender body, narrow feet, long legs, small arms, and a long stiff tail.
facts.quote: Media cerca de 3,5 metros de largo y pesaba cerca de 475 kilogramos, tenía un cuerpo delgado y pies angostos, con las piernas largas, las brazos pequeños, y una cola larga y tiesa.

facts.statement: It is believed that Claosaurus moved on two legs but supported itself on all four limbs while feeding.
facts.quote: Se cree que se movilizaba en dos patas y solo se apoyaba sobre sus cuatro miembros para alimentarse.

facts.statement: A 2008 analysis found Claosaurus agilis outside the clade containing Hadrosaurus and other hadrosaurids, making it the closest non-hadrosaurid relative to true hadrosaurids within Hadrosauria.
facts.quote: Tradicionalmente clasificado como un miembro basal de la familia Hadrosauridae, un análisis de 2008 halló que Claosaurus agilis estaba fuera del clado que contenía Hadrosaurus y otros hadrosáuridos, por lo que es el pariente no hadrosáurido más cercano a los hadrosáuridos verdaderos dentro del clado Hadrosauria.

rejected.statement: It is more likely that the supposed gastroliths found in the misidentified specimen represent gravel washed in during burial rather than stomach stones.
rejected.quote: Additionally, it is more likely that the supposed gastroliths represent gravel washed in during burial.
